cards.text: New campsite, friend. In the first month, the whole congregation of Israel comes into the Wilderness of Zin and stays in Kadesh. And there, the camp says goodbye to someone.

cards.question: While Israel stays at Kadesh, someone dies and is buried there. Who is it?

cards.text: Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron (Numbers 26:59), is buried there at Kadesh. Then the camp runs into the one problem a wilderness just LOVES to hand you.

cards.question: At Kadesh, there is no ___ for the congregation.
With no water at Kadesh, the congregation gathers to pray alongside Moses and Aaron.

cards.text: The people quarrel with Moses and say, "If only we had perished with our brothers before the LORD!" Friend, I know that voice. One flat batch and I'm draped across the counter going, "Just leave me here. Tell the oven I loved it."

cards.question: The people ask Moses why he brought the LORD's assembly into this wilderness for them and their livestock to ___ there.
Next the people ask Moses why he led them up out of ___ to this wretched place.

cards.text: Then they list what this place is not: not a place of grain, figs, vines or pomegranates, "and there is no water to drink!" Moses and Aaron leave the assembly, go to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and fall facedown.

cards.question: Moses and Aaron are facedown at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. What appears to them?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses: take the staff and assemble the congregation. An AUDIENCE, friend? Put one baker in front of me and I can't stamp straight. Last time somebody watched, I stamped the counter.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses and Aaron to do something to the rock while the congregation watches, and it will pour out its water. What is it?

cards.text: So Moses takes the staff from the LORD's presence, just as he had been commanded. He and Aaron gather the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses starts talking.

cards.question: In front of the rock, Moses asks the assembly, "must we bring you water out of this rock?" But first, what does Moses call them?
Then Moses raises his hand and ___ the rock ___ with his staff.
After Moses strikes the rock, a great amount of water gushes out, and the congregation and their livestock are able to drink.

cards.text: Water's gushing, everybody's drinking. Then the LORD speaks to Moses and Aaron, and it is NOT a thank-you note.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses and Aaron what they did not do at the rock. What was it?

answers.text: Trust Him to show His holiness
Thank Him in front of the people
Ask Him which rock to use

cards.question: Even after the rock, the LORD says Moses and Aaron will still be the ones who bring the assembly into the land He has given them.

cards.text: "These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them." Write that name on the box, friend: Meribah.

findings.problem: The joke 'Last time somebody watched, I stamped the counter' sits right before Moses strikes the rock. It hints that pressure from an audience made him hit the wrong thing. The text never gives a reason for the strike, and the line also points toward the answer on card 15.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Card 11 gives nothing the baker can use to reason out that the LORD says to speak to the rock. 'Pray beside it' and 'Stand on it' are just as likely from what's been told, so this key moment comes down to luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The turning point of the passage has no setup card. After card 14, nothing helps the baker reason toward 'struck' over 'touched', or 'twice' over 'once', so both blanks are luck. With cards 2, 10, 12 and 14 also being discovery questions, discovery is close to half the stop instead of 'a few'.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The sentence mixes tenses: 'Moses raises his hand and ___ the rock ___ with his staff' has a present-tense 'raises' but the past-tense answers 'struck' and 'touched'.
findings.question: Should fill-in-the-blank sentences keep one tense throughout, by using 'strikes' and 'touches', or by putting the whole sentence in past tense to match the BSB wording?

findings.problem: 'Thank Him in front of the people' and 'Ask Him which rock to use' are both things Moses and Aaron never do in the passage. A baker could argue either one answers 'what they did not do at the rock.'

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Trust Him to show His holiness', uses the passage's own wording and sounds like the Bible. The two wrong answers sound plain and everyday, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Story cards 1, 9, 13 and 20 are almost straight retelling with little of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 13 in particular is just the verse paraphrased. Real laughs show up only on cards 6, 11 and 17.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
